row_traceability.boundary: Exact source-scoped identifiers anchor legal identity; names and fuzzy matches remain candidates and cannot silently merge entities.
Literature supports preserving meaning and documenting absence; the exact observed/zero/blank/none-stated/not-applicable/not-reported/not-found-publicly/invalid taxonomy is a project design choice.

row_traceability.semantic_control: Publication, effective, retrieval and cutoff time
row_traceability.boundary: Value period and each availability/retrieval/cutoff timestamp remain separate so later evidence cannot support an earlier claim.
Corrections and semantic changes create new versions; earlier evidence bytes and historical information boundaries are not overwritten.
Quality dimensions and rules are evaluated for a named data object and reporting task; no context-free aggregate score establishes universal fitness.

limitations: The exhibit is an author synthesis and design rationale, not implementation or evaluation results.
The exact missing-state taxonomy is a project design choice; literature supports preserving semantic absence but does not publish this exact universal set.
The compact table omits additional connector-specific operational states documented elsewhere in the project.
An exact identifier reduces identity ambiguity but does not establish economic activity or the truth of every record attached to that identifier.
A matching checksum establishes byte identity and traceability, not source correctness or fitness for every reporting use.
Availability and correction handling remain claim- and cutoff-specific; current evidence cannot be projected retrospectively.
The exhibit contains no mutable corpus count, result value, measured performance, production claim or universal quality score.
